title: Phantom Blade Zero Boss Guide - Rules, Regions and the Fights That Stop Runs
description: How boss fights work in Phantom Blade Zero: the red, blue and purple flash tells, the Sha-Chi loop, and where every one of the 59 documented bosses sits by region.

sections.title: The Short Answer
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero has 59 documented boss encounters across nine regions: 33 on the critical path and 24 optional. Published counts range from 50 to 62 because some lists fold in rematches, so the number you see elsewhere is not wrong so much as counting something different.

This page is the hub: the rules that apply to every fight, then the route into the full roster by region and the individual fights worth reading up on before you walk in.

sections.title: The Three Colours That Decide Every Fight
sections.content:
There is no elemental weakness system, so the usual resistance tables do not apply. What the game uses instead is a colour language on enemy attacks, and it is the single most valuable thing to internalise:

TellMeaningAnswer
Red flashUnblockable attackDodge — guarding does nothing
Blue flashParryable attackDeflect for the fastest Sha-Chi drain
Purple flashThe boss just parried youStop attacking; a counter is coming

The purple flash is the one that ends runs, because it looks like an opening. See the combat system for how Sha-Chi, Ghoststep and guard breaks fit together.

sections.title: What Works on Almost Everything
sections.content:
• Deflect blue flashes to drain Sha-Chi — it is the fastest way to open a damage window, faster than hitting.
  • Dodge red flashes instead of blocking. Every guide that mentions the system says the same thing.
  • Break guard with Sha-Chi attacks rather than chipping health through a raised guard.
  • Swap weapons mid-fight: switching refills stamina, which is what keeps a combo alive.
  • Hold Power Surge for the window you have already created, never to create one.
  • When a boss will not take damage at all, look for the smoke or shimmer effect — that is an invulnerability state you have to break, not out-damage.

sections.title: The Fights That Actually Stop People
sections.content:
• Gu Wanyue — immune until the Sha-Chi bar breaks
  • Wu Lengshuang — a parry duel with a purple-flash counter
  • Bai Chilian — the attack set changes mid-fight
  • Bi Feng — sweeping attacks and a guard that has to be broken
  • Lei Dang — two phases, and the Tiger Cannon behind them
  • Zuo Shang — the true-ending final boss

Everything else in the roster folds into two habits: read the flash colour, and stop pressing attack when the boss tells you to stop.

sections.title: Which Boss Ends Which Ending
sections.content: The normal ending closes on Meng Hua; the true ending continues past her to Zuo Shang, The True Long, and the final scripted encounter only fires if the true-ending checklist is complete. The requirements are on the true ending page, and the four endings themselves are on endings.

sections.title: Sources
sections.content: Roster, locations and drops are compiled from published post-launch guides (NoobFeed, Game8, GamesRadar, 游侠网) and cross-checked against each other; where they disagree the individual fight page says so. Attack patterns and colour tells are only written where a guide describes the fight — the 2 encounters without published notes are marked as unconfirmed rather than filled with filler.
